newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico rebels denounce human rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebels denounce human rights abuses.

text.p: Rebels of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) on Sunday denounced human rights abuses by the Mexican government in its hunt for the Marxist group and said the army had tortured an EPR fighter.

In a statement obtained by Reuters, the EPR said three people in the poor, western state of Guerrero had been "disappeared" by the army in the past few months. "Disappeared" is a euphemism for kidnapping and usually death at the hands of security forces.

It also said peasant farmers in the southern state of Oaxaca suspected of belonging to the EPR had been dangled outside army helicopters in the air and forced into signing confessions that they were rebel sympathisers.

"In our country, the human rights situation has deteriorated ... Just a few months ago, the president of Mexico pledged the EPR would be fought without resorting to human rights abuses," the EPR said in the statement signed by Commanders "Antonio" and "Hermenegildo."
Officials at the Defence Ministry were not available for comment on the EPR statement.
The rebel group, which first appeared in June, said one of its members, "Rafael," is being tortured at the hands of the army and demanded the army give proof he is alive.
It said Rafael was captured by three unidentified men on Oct. 25, a few days before state officials acknowledged the army had captured the EPR fighter.

"Knowing the history of torture ... inflicted upon political prisoners and given the fact he has not been seen alive, we denounce that our fighter is being subjected to inhumane methods of interrogation and fear for his life," the EPR said.

Dozens of EPR guerrillas have appeared in a handful of villages throughout the state in the past few days, peacefully handing out propaganda and urging locals to join their fight against the government of President Ernesto Zedillo.
At least 25 people have died in EPR attacks in several central and southern Mexican states since June.
